bottlenecks.problem: Impact assessment takes 7 to 12 business days, almost all of it waiting for SME e-mail responses.
bottlenecks.cause: Functional input is requested by unstructured e-mail with a 5-day SLA; the QA Analyst averages 3.2 follow-ups per SME and must reconcile conflicting answers in meetings. Affected documents are found by manually searching spreadsheets rather than by content.
bottlenecks.suggested_improvement: An Impact Assessment Agent pre-identifies affected SOPs, products and systems by semantic search across the DMS and eQMS, drafts the IA form and sends SMEs a structured confirm/adjust task with a 2-day SLA and automated reminders. SMEs validate rather than research.

bottlenecks.problem: Controlled document revision takes 10 to 15 business days per change with 1.4 formatting/citation errors per document set.
bottlenecks.cause: Authors draft redlines by hand for an average of 4 documents; Document Control then checks numbering and cross-references manually; errors found at QA review trigger another cycle.
bottlenecks.suggested_improvement: A Documentation Drafting Agent generates first-pass redlines that insert the regulatory requirement into each affected document and validates cross-references, numbering and citations before routing to the document owner and QA for approval.

bottlenecks.problem: Change Requests wait an average of 4.5 business days for the weekly CCB, and 20% are returned and re-presented the following week.
bottlenecks.cause: Approval is tied to a fixed Tuesday meeting cadence rather than to readiness; incomplete packs are only discovered in the meeting.
bottlenecks.frequency: Every Medium/High risk change; 20% incur a second week
bottlenecks.suggested_improvement: Replace the weekly meeting with asynchronous CCB e-voting inside the eQMS with a 48-hour SLA, fed by an AI-generated briefing pack that has passed completeness checks. Part 11 signatures and the approve/reject decision remain fully human.

bottlenecks.problem: Each logged item requires 2 to 4 hours of full-document reading, and Not Applicable decisions wait up to 5 business days for RA Manager countersignature.
bottlenecks.cause: Applicability is determined by a specialist reading every source document in full; there is no pre-screening against the product, site and registration inventory.
bottlenecks.frequency: ~40 items per week; ~92% end as Not Applicable
bottlenecks.suggested_improvement: An Applicability Screening Agent compares each update against the registration and product inventory, proposes Applicable / Not Applicable with rationale and confidence, and routes low-confidence or applicable items to the RA Specialist. High-confidence Not Applicable items are batch-countersigned weekly.

bottlenecks.problem: Approximately 40 regulatory items per week are monitored, downloaded and logged by hand, and only 71% of applicable updates are captured within 2 business days.
bottlenecks.cause: Daily manual review of five source types and an e-mail digest, with metadata re-typed into an Excel log.
bottlenecks.frequency: Daily; ~13 hours of effort per week
bottlenecks.suggested_improvement: A Regulatory Intake Agent monitors the sources, de-duplicates, extracts metadata (authority, type, dates, affected topics) and writes the RIL entry and archive automatically within hours of publication.

bottlenecks.problem: Compliance review takes 3 to 5 business days and averages 1.6 cycles before all comments are closed.
bottlenecks.cause: Reviewers discover gaps in regulatory interpretation, ALCOA+ coverage and action completeness only after the CR is submitted; there is no pre-submission check.
bottlenecks.frequency: Every change; 60% need a second cycle
bottlenecks.suggested_improvement: A Compliance Pre-Review Agent checks the CR against the regulatory text, internal policy library and data-integrity checklist and flags gaps to the Process Owner before submission. The Compliance Officer and RA Manager review a clean pack and retain the decision.

bottlenecks.problem: A 1 to 2 hour risk classification waits 2 to 3 business days for QA Manager availability.
bottlenecks.cause: Classification criteria are rule-like (ICH Q9 categories) but the task is queued behind the manager's calendar.
bottlenecks.suggested_improvement: A Risk Classification Agent proposes Low / Medium / High with rationale mapped to the SOP criteria; the QA Manager confirms from a prioritised approval queue. The decision and accountability remain with the QA Manager.

bottlenecks.problem: About 60% of Change Request creation effort is re-typing data already captured in the Impact Assessment and Regulatory Summary.
bottlenecks.cause: The IA form (Word/PDF), the RIL (Excel) and the eQMS are disconnected, so 14 mandatory fields are populated manually.
bottlenecks.suggested_improvement: Automatically create the CR from the structured IA and Regulatory Summary, attach source documents and pre-populate the action plan; the Process Owner reviews and submits.

bottlenecks.problem: Training runs 20 to 30 calendar days with 4 to 6 hours of coordinator effort spent on manual reminders and completion reporting.
bottlenecks.cause: Assignment, weekly monitoring, reminders and escalation are performed by hand from LMS exports.
bottlenecks.suggested_improvement: Automate assignment from the curriculum matrix, reminders and the 95% completion escalation rule. The 30-day effective-date window is a policy control and is retained; only the coordination effort is removed.

summary: Elapsed time is dominated by waiting rather than work: SME coordination (7-12 days), document revision (10-15 days), the weekly CCB cadence (4.5 days plus 20% re-presentation), compliance review cycles (3-5 days) and manager availability for risk classification (2-3 days). Effort is dominated by high-volume manual screening of ~40 regulatory items a week, of which ~92% are not applicable. Duplicate data entry between the RIL, IA form and eQMS adds rework and error opportunities.
